title: Anti-Abortion Groups Announce Major $4.5M Campaign - NewsBreak
text:
By Roger Anderson ,
6 hours ago Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America and Women Speak Out PAC have launched a $4.5 million campaign targeting Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-GA) over his abortion record. The effort aims to spotlight Ossoff’s stance on reproductive rights and sway voters ahead of upcoming elections. The effort targets Savannah, Augusta, Columbus, and Chattanooga, aiming to reach 1 million voters before the 2026 midterms. Ossoff’s campaign has responded to the ad campaign. Spokeswoman Ellie Dougherty stated that the ads signal Republicans’ intent to “further rip away women’s health care access at every turn,” adding that the campaign is “building unstoppable momentum to win next November and stop the GOP’s methodical anti-abortion efforts in its tracks.”
Susan B. Anthony Pro‑Life America cited Ossoff’s votes supporting abortion funding, while President Marjorie Dannenfelser called him a “pro‑abortion radical.”
Dannenfelser said, “If Senator Ossoff thinks he can hide from his record of voting in lock step with the brutal abortion industry 100 percent of the time, he should think again. He is a pro-abortion radical and must be defeated.”
Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America Atlanta field director Jillian Wooton said, “We’re on fire for the next big phase in the battle for life.”
Wooton added, “As we lost a hero of the pro-life movement when Charlie Kirk was killed, each of us is more determined than ever to speak up boldly. By reaching voters and winning elections, we have the opportunity to protect the lives of countless babies and serve their moms, too.”
The state supreme court previously reinstated a six-week abortion ban, and Republicans are now eyeing potential Ossoff challengers. Potential candidates include Reps. Buddy Carter, Mike Collins, and Derek Dooley.
Dannenfelser said, “Not only did he back a national mandate for all-trimester abortion — he even vetoed a bill simply requiring life-saving care for babies born alive after an attempted abortion.”
Roger Anderson covers U.S. politics & news for content partner Modern Newsstand LLC.
